articles.title: Download now
articles.description: Top stories, breaking news, live reporting, and follow news topics that match your interests

articles.title: Judge Allows Trump’s Defamation Lawsuit Against the BBC to Proceed
articles.description: President Trump is seeking damages from the British broadcaster over a documentary it conceded was misleadingly edited.

articles.title: Alexander Darchiev, Russia’s Ambassador to the U.S., Dies at 66
articles.description: The death of Alexander Darchiev was announced by Russia’s foreign ministry. He was appointed to his post in Washington in 2025, as relations between the Kremlin and the White House warmed.

articles.title: Protesters Throw Projectiles at Biden During Dublin Trip
articles.description: Video showed demonstrators from a pro-Palestinian protest throwing projectiles at former President Joseph R. Biden Jr. after he attended an event at Trinity College Dublin on Tuesday.

articles.title: U.S. Efforts to Tighten Blockade of Iran Rely on Reluctant Neighbors
articles.description: Washington wants to intensify its economic pressure campaign on Iran by closing its land borders. Neighboring states, fearing economic fallout, are pushing back.

articles.title: Kenya Starts Countdown to End of Ebola Outbreak
articles.description: The milestone is further evidence that African countries have mostly succeeded in preventing community transmission and isolating the small number of cases that have come in from Congo.

articles.title: Seeking to Broaden Ukraine Talks, U.S. Urges Russia to Include Europe
articles.description: As a round of negotiations ended in Abu Dhabi, President Trump’s envoys said they would go to Moscow as the Kremlin demands discussions on European security structures.

articles.title: Lots of Competition to Catholicism in Peru as Pope Returns for Visit
articles.description: Pope Leo spent nearly two decades in Peru, rising to bishop and becoming a citizen. But many Peruvians have turned to evangelical churches, seeking a more expressive and direct connection to God.

articles.title: In Interview, Sonia Gandhi Recalls Love and Loss in India
articles.description: In a memoir and interview, the Italian-born woman who married into the Nehru-Gandhi dynasty recalls political battles and the killings of family members.

articles.title: A Museum’s ‘Wanted’ Poster Campaign Brings Looted Painting Back to France
articles.description: The Orléans Fine Arts Museum is on a quest to recover hundreds of works stolen during World War II — and the director wants your help.

articles.title: Lebanon Faces Economic ‘Catastrophe’ After War and Years of Mismanagement
articles.description: Hezbollah’s conflict with Israel and the U.S.-Israel war with Iran have made systemic problems worse, causing the cost of living to soar and driving many Lebanese to despair.

articles.title: Canadian Authorities Kill 4 Bears Involved in Deadly Attack on Hikers
articles.description: Wildlife authorities said evidence, including animal DNA, conclusively linked a sow and her three cubs to the deaths of two women along a hiking trail in British Columbia.

articles.title: No Good Choices on Iran
articles.description: As top Trump aides clash over a strategy to end the war, the administration is weighing escalation, narrower strikes and diplomacy.

articles.title: ICE Deportation Flight Carrying Iranians Turns Back and Lands in Arizona
articles.description: The Iranian immigrants in the plane were scheduled to be flown to Pakistan and then transferred to Iran, lawyers for the group said.

articles.title: Israeli Opposition Pushes for Oct. 7 Inquiry at First Session of New Parliament
articles.description: Dozens of first-time lawmakers were sworn into the Knesset, where the opposition, led by Gadi Eisenkot, now has a majority.

articles.title: The mammoth effort to entomb the ruins of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant
articles.description: Film following the team racing to entomb the ruins of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant.

articles.title: Meghan Markle Makes First Public Appearance Since Her Father’s Arrest
articles.description: The Duchess of Sussex accompanied her husband, Prince Harry, in Brussels at an event about online safety for children.

articles.title: Novaya Gazeta, Russia’s Bravest Newspaper, Closes
articles.description: For more than 30 years, the paper covered an increasingly repressive Russia. “The process of silencing us started many years ago,” one of its journalists said.

articles.title: Rubio Says ‘Major Combat Operations’ in Iran War Are No Longer Needed
articles.description: The U.S. secretary of state said that American economic pressure is doing sufficient damage to the leadership in Tehran.

articles.title: In Argentina, Pope Leo Walks in the Giant Shadow of Francis
articles.description: Francis never returned to his home country after becoming pope, but the new pontiff will still be confronted with the overwhelming presence of his predecessor.

articles.title: Gaza Floods Kill 4
articles.description: At least four people from one family died and thousands lost their shelters when a storm battered overcrowded tent camps. Israel says Gaza will not be rebuilt until Hamas disarms.

articles.title: David Walliams, UK Celebrity, Is Accused of Sexual Misconduct
articles.description: The Guardian and ITV News published claims from multiple women against the comedian and writer, who fought a weekslong court battle to keep the claims private. He denies the accusations.

articles.title: Syria Weighs Sending Troops to Aid Saudi War With Houthis
articles.description: Syrian reconnaissance teams have visited Saudi Arabia and Yemen ahead of a potential deployment, but a final decision has not been made, officials said.

articles.title: Jemima Goldsmith, Russell Brand’s Ex-Partner, Accuses Him of Abuse
articles.description: Ms. Goldsmith, a British TV producer, accused Mr. Brand of “violence” and “coercive control” during their relationship. She made the allegations publicly for the first time after his sentencing for rape and sexual assault.

articles.title: U.S. Received $12 Billion From Venezuela’s Oil, Report Shows
articles.description: The workings of a U.S.-controlled bank account shed light on how Washington manages Venezuelan revenue after capturing the country’s president.

articles.title: What to Know About Thomas Massie, Leader of Drive to Impeach Hegseth
articles.description: Representative Thomas Massie, Republican of Kentucky, is retiring at the end of his term after losing to a primary challenger backed by President Trump.

articles.title: Najib Razak, Ex-Prime Minister of Malaysia, Is Released to House Arrest
articles.description: Najib Razak, who was brought down in the multibillion-dollar 1MDB scandal, was released from prison to serve the rest of his sentence in his mansion.

articles.title: U.S. Forces in Europe Face Uncertainty as Pentagon Reviews Troop Levels
articles.description: A U.S. Army unit in Germany is not sure what’s next as the Pentagon considers a major drawdown of forces in Europe.

articles.title: Why U.S. Business Deals Are Unlikely to Get Putin to Give Any Ground
articles.description: President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia has shown a willingness to endure a high price to get what he wants in Ukraine, and he sees little reason to stop fighting now, analysts say.

articles.title: Who Is David Walliams, the UK Entertainer Accused of Sexual Misconduct?
articles.description: The British entertainer rose to fame with the television show “Little Britain” and has published over 40 children’s books.

articles.title: Australia Unveils New A.I. Regulator After OpenAI Breach
articles.description: The government is also considering changes to criminal law to penalize companies that develop models that “engage in harmful conduct.”

articles.title: As Fresh Air Becomes a Luxury, Many Indonesians Turn on Their Leader
articles.description: In Indonesia, support for President Prabowo Subianto has collapsed as his government has failed to contain raging wildfires, compounding quality-of-life woes.

articles.title: Indonesia’s Vice President, Gibran, Resigns
articles.description: Gibran Rakabuming Raka, who is stepping down amid a scandal over his academic credentials, was a symbol of the partnership that elevated President Prabowo Subianto into office.

articles.title: Nvidia Scandal Unleashes a Flood of AI-Generated Memes
articles.description: The revelations surrounding Jensen Huang, who resigned from Nvidia over extramarital affairs, inspired social media posts using the very technology his company helped develop.

articles.title: Army Officer Accused of Trying to Spy for Russia Is Afghan War Veteran
articles.description: The officer, who served at a NATO base in Britain, is expected to be charged in the coming days, two officials said.

articles.title: Where does record-breaking Kane rank among all-time England greats?
articles.description: Harry Kane is England's all-time top scorer and record appearance maker, but where does he rank among the Three Lions' greatest players?

articles.title: The Man Who Helped the C.I.A. Secretly Operate in Mexico
articles.description: President Claudia Sheinbaum drew a firm line barring U.S. forces from operating on Mexican soil. But in a northern border state, one local partner quietly helped the agency build a foothold.

articles.title: Mexican Prosecutor Who Helped C.I.A. Secretly Operate in His State Flees to the U.S.
articles.description: The prosecutor, who faces arrest in Mexico after allowing C.I.A. officers into Chihuahua state, is under the protection of the U.S. government, according to U.S. and Mexican officials.

articles.title: Weekly quiz: Who's joining Wayne Rooney in the I'm A Celebrity jungle?
articles.description: How much attention did you pay to what happened in the world over the past seven days?

articles.title: A Key Paris Agreement Goal Is Dead. What Now?
articles.description: Leaders at COP31 are confronting a new reality as global warming enters the “unsafe zone.”

articles.title: Israeli Strikes on Gaza Hospital Kill 6 and Injure Dozens, Health Officials Say
articles.description: The Israeli authorities said that Hamas had established a command center at the hospital complex. Hamas said the attack was “a heinous crime targeting a civilian medical facility.”

articles.title: Israel’s Arrest of Journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh Raises Concerns
articles.description: Abed Abu Shehadeh, a Palestinian citizen of Israel, was detained without being charged with a crime, raising concerns that the domestic security service is overstepping its authority.

articles.title: On Dakar’s Packed Beaches, Africa Welcomes Its First Youth Olympics
articles.description: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games are taking place in Senegal, where the beaches and streets are teeming with sports fans and fitness fanatics.

articles.title: A.I. Weapons Need Data for Their Training. Ukraine Has a Lot to Offer.
articles.description: The Ukrainian government has opened up a trove of five million battlefield videos to defense companies at home and abroad.

articles.title: They Left Iran, but Now the Regime Is Seizing Their Assets to Silence Them
articles.description: The Iranian authorities are pursuing diaspora dissidents and journalists, extending the government’s repressive apparatus far beyond its borders.

articles.title: This Defense Makes Drones (and GPS) Think They’re in Peru
articles.description: GPS-linked devices have been insisting that Ukrainians are in Lima, the Peruvian capital. The culprit is a jamming system built to thwart Russian airstrikes.

articles.title: Workers in Spain Stage a General Strike for the First Time in 14 Years
articles.description: Workers in a wide range of industries walked off the job to protest rising rents and stagnant wages, which have become central issues in the campaign.

articles.title: A.I. and Market Whiplash
articles.description: A Times reporter who covers financial markets helps us make sense of tech turbulence.

articles.title: She Is Rewriting Mexico’s Ballads, One Woman’s Story at a Time
articles.description: Grammy-nominated songwriter Vivir Quintana is known throughout Latin America for giving voice to women who fought back against domestic violence.

articles.title: Nvidia Scandal Unveils a Fierce Spy War Raging Behind Trump and Xi’s Diplomacy
articles.description: That the United States suspected Nvidia’s leader was a Chinese spy target underscores the deep distrust between the two powers, even as their leaders try to stabilize ties.
